glosses: to persuade, to talk (into), to urge
убеждать, заставлять согласиться с кем-либо или с чем-либо, склонять к чему-либо

examples.text: Меня все уговаривали последовать благому примеру, ― а пуще всех сердце; но зная, что завтра достанется мне в дежурство, я не мог и не хотел согласиться.

glosses: устар. успокаивать, утешать

examples.text: Вот эта девушка будто и плачет; а одна дама, такая почтенная, уговаривает ее и обнимает, а она все плачет; да и кавалер этот неспокоен: он все ходит будто в отчаянии; не знаю, тут что-то карета сделала.

glosses: перен., жарг. выпивать полностью (бутылку спиртного)

examples.text: Они выпивали и закусывали. Иногда уговаривали целую бутылку. Принимались за песню.

glosses: To successfully convince (someone) to agree to, accept, or do something, usually through reasoning and verbal influence.

examples.text: That salesman was able to persuade me into buying this bottle of lotion.

[VV]e are able with playne demonſtration to proue, and vvith reaſon to perſvvade that in tymes paſt our fayth vvas alike, that then vve preached thinges correſpondent vnto the forme of faith already published of vs, ſo that none in this behalfe can repyne or gaynesay vs.
We will persuade him, be it possible.

The boy became volubly friendly and bubbling over with unexpected humour and high spirits. He tried to persuade Cicely to stay away from the ball-room for a fourth dance. Nobody would miss them, he explained.

The most persistent tormentor was Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, who scored a hat-trick in last month’s corresponding fixture in Iceland. His ability to run at defences is instantly striking, but it is his clever use of possession that has persuaded some shrewd judges that he is an even better prospect than Theo Walcott.

glosses: To convince of by argument, or by reasons offered or suggested from reflection, etc.; to cause to believe (something).

examples.text: But beloued, wee are perswaded better things of you, and things that accompany saluation, though we thus speake.

glosses: To urge, plead; to try to convince (someone to do something).

examples.text: […] and hearken not vnto Hezekiah, when hee perswadeth you, saying, The Lord will deliuer vs.
She did not go into the coffee-room, though repeatedly persuaded by Miss Woodley, but waited at the door till her carriage drew up.
He persuaded me to go home, but I refused.
He did not persuade me long before I consented.

glosses: To communicate, usually by means of speech.

examples.text: Let's sit down and talk.
Although I don't speak Chinese, I managed to talk with the villagers using signs and gestures.
I will buy with you, sell with you, talk with you, walk with you, and so following, but I will not eat with you.

Then he commenced to talk, really talk. and inside of two flaps of a herring's fin he had me mesmerized, like Eben Holt's boy at the town hall show. He talked about the ills of humanity, and the glories of health and Nature and service and land knows what all. […] It was a chance he was offering me, a wonderful, eighteen carat, solid gold chance.
Mr. Campion appeared suitably impressed and she warmed to him. He was very easy to talk to with those long clown lines in his pale face, a natural goon, born rather too early she suspected.
Let’s go to my office and talk. ― I like to talk with you, Ms. Weaver.

“[…] They talk of you as if you were Croesus—and I expect the beggars sponge on you unconscionably.” And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his platform utterances. He spoke with extreme contempt of the dense stupidity exhibited on all occasions by the working classes.

glosses: To discuss; to talk about.

examples.text: They sat down to talk business.
That's enough about work, let's talk holidays!

glosses: To speak (a certain language).

examples.text: We talk French sometimes.

glosses: Used to emphasise the importance, size, complexity etc. of the thing mentioned.

examples.text: Are you interested in the job? They're talking big money.
We're not talking rocket science here: it should be easy.

glosses: To confess, especially implicating others.

examples.text: Suppose he talks?
She can be relied upon not to talk.
They tried to make me talk.

glosses: To criticize someone for something of which one is guilty oneself.

examples.text: Look who's talking.
I am not the one to talk.
She is a fine one to talk.
You should talk.

glosses: To gossip; to create scandal.

examples.text: People will talk.
Aren't you afraid the neighbours will talk?

glosses: To manifest outwardly in speech, as opposed to reality or action.

examples.text: Remember that Christ and Christianity may not always be the same thing; e.g. Jerry Falwell talks "Christianity" but practices hatred […] which is diametrically opposed to what Jesus really taught.

glosses: To influence someone to express something, especially a particular stance or viewpoint or in a particular manner.

examples.text: That's not like you at all, Jared. The drugs are talking. Snap out of it!

"So, are you going to give up all this good living and easy money and come fly for the Russians?"
"Hello no. I told you that yesterday."

glosses: A conversation or discussion; usually serious, but informal.

examples.text: We need to have a talk about your homework.

All this was extraordinarily distasteful to Churchill.[…]Never before had he felt such repulsion when the vicar displayed his characteristic bluntness or coarseness of speech. In the present connection—or rather as a transition from the subject that started their conversation—such talk had been distressingly out of place.

glosses: A lecture.

examples.text: There is a talk on Shakespeare tonight.

glosses: Gossip; rumour.

examples.text: There's been talk lately about the two of them.

glosses: A major topic of social discussion.

examples.text: She is the talk of the day.
The musical is the talk of the town.

glosses: A customary conversation by parent(s) or guardian(s) with their (often teenage) child about a reality of life; in particular:
A customary conversation in which parent(s) explain sexual intercourse to their child.

examples.text: Have you had the talk with Jay yet? I found a condom in his room.

glosses: A customary conversation by parent(s) or guardian(s) with their (often teenage) child about a reality of life; in particular:
A customary conversation in which the parent(s) of a black child explain the racism and violence they may face, especially when interacting with police, and strategies to manage it.

examples.text: Later, I made sure to have the talk with my son about being a black boy, […]
All the black parents I have ever spoken to have had “the talk” with their sons and daughters. “The talk” is a conversation about how to behave and not to behave with police.
Now, I was a black man in the South, and my folks had had “the talk” with me. No, not the one about the birds and bees. This one is about the black man and the police.

glosses: Empty boasting, promises or claims.

examples.text: The party leader's speech was all talk.

glosses: Meeting to discuss a particular matter.

examples.text: The leaders of the G8 nations are currently in talks over nuclear weapons.

glosses: To lead by persuasion or influence; incite or prevail upon.

examples.text: The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track. The three returned wondering and charmed with Mrs. Cooke; they were sure she had had no hand in the furnishing of that atrocious house.

glosses: To cause, bring about, lead to.

examples.text: His meditation induced a compromise. Opium induces sleep.
A mere glance at the plot descriptions of the show’s fourth season is enough to induce Pavlovian giggle fits and shivers of joy.

glosses: To induce the labour of (a pregnant woman).

examples.text: By the time of my third, five months ago, I was a right bossy cow about what I wanted because I knew the drill. For reasons I shan’t bore you with, I got them to induce me at 39 weeks, at 10am, with the epidural going in first, and it was all a dream.

glosses: To cause or produce (electric current or a magnetic state) by a physical process of induction.

examples.text: The scientific instruments of the day recorded rapid fluctuations in the Earth's magnetic field, as powerful electrical currents flowed through the upper atmosphere. Ships' logs noted observations of the northern lights as far south as the Caribbean, and telegraph systems across the world were disrupted as electrical currents were induced in the copper lines.

glosses: To infer by induction.
To lead in, bring in, introduce.
To draw on, place upon.

examples.text: satisfy your urges
After seeing the advert for a soft drink, I had a sudden urge to buy a bottle.
sexual urges
repress your urges
Unless I’m wrong / I but obey / The urge of a song: / I’m—bound—away!

glosses: To press; to push; to drive; to impel; to force onward.

examples.text: Lo hapless Tydeus, whose ill-fated hand / Had slain his brother, leaves his native land, / And seized with horror in the shades of night, / Through the thick deserts headlong urged his flight[…]

glosses: To put mental pressure on; to ply with motives, arguments, persuasion, or importunity.

examples.text: My boss urged me to reconsider my decision to leave the company, even offering a pay rise.

You do miſtake your buſines, my Brother neuer / Did vrge me in his Act : I did inquire it, / And haue my Learning from ſome true reports / That drew their ſwords with you, did he not rather / Diſcredit my authority with yours, / And make the warres alike againſt my ſtomacke, / Hauing alike your cauſe.

glosses: To provoke; to exasperate.

examples.text: Vrge not my fathers anger (Eglamoure) / But thinke vpon my griefe (a Ladies griefe) / And on the iuſtice of my flying hence, / To keepe me from a moſt vnholy match, / Which heauen and fortune ſtill rewards with plagues.

glosses: To press hard upon; to follow closely.

examples.text: Man ? and for ever ? wretch ! what wouldst thou have ? / Heir urges heir, like wave impelling wave.

examples.text: to urge an argument; to urge the necessity of a case

glosses: To treat with forcible means; to take severe or violent measures with.

examples.text: to urge an ore with intense heat

glosses: To press onward or forward.

examples.text: Bien plus, l’expérience de tant de lois rendues en divers temps, en divers pays, contre la brigue et la subornation, nous convainquent qu’il n’y a point de remède direct contre la corruption électorale, aucun moyen de la rendre atteignable sous toutes ses formes.

examples.text: Citoyen islandais, M. Jón Kristinsson fut convaincu en 1984 de deux infractions au code de la route par le tribunal correctionnel du district d’Akureyri, qui lui infligea une amende.

examples.text: Mon cher lecteur, pleurez avec ces éplorés, si cela peut vous faire plaisir, mais soyez bien persuadé que ces pleureurs ne sont pas les représentants de l'esprit ni du caractère liégeois.

examples.text: Persuader une vérité à quelqu’un.

examples.text: Il essaya de se persuader qu’il était à l’aise et en sécurité ; mais bientôt, l’indéfinissable inquiétude de l’animal sociable, abandonné dans la solitude, le tourmenta.

examples.text: L’ouvrier se sert d'une lame courte et tranchante, engagée dans un manche d’os, avec laquelle il pratique, au bas de l’arbre, une entaille circulaire et assez profonde pour arriver jusqu'à l’aubier.

examples.text: — Venez dîner après-demain, je vais l’engager ; il ne me refuse jamais, et il refuse presque toujours madame de Puylaurens.
